thread:
shera: Heads-up — over the last 18m SFO edge started evicting a subset of GPU pods (mostly p3-type slices) when autoscaler hit cold-start limits. We saw a steady rise in 429s and tail latency for realtime routes. Rolling traffic to AMS avoided hard failure but latency spiked. Took node-level drains and rebalanced slices.

mike: How widespread? percent of capacity lost?

shera: ~14% of SFO reserved pool (hot slice group). Evictions were correlated with a burst of new node provisioning + kubelet churn. Logs show kubelet restarted on 6 nodes within a 2m window.

infra-bot: alert: SFO_NODE_RESTART_RATE > 5/min on nodegroup gpu-pool-3
infra-bot: metric snapshot: p95 latency realtime=720ms, 429s=3.2%, active_pods_evicted=28

elaine: We ran the "soft-drain -> replace" sequence from the docs and rebalanced traffic via weighted-traffic-shift (10% steps to AMS). Canary held. No data plane errors beyond client timeouts.

nate: Sounds like we need two runbook updates: 1) add a cooldown guard on autoscaler to avoid overlapping node boots + pod evictions, 2) change reserve-pool ordering so warm pool heals before spilling to shared capacity. Current ordering causes hot-slice loss during simultaneous node churn.

amanda: I can author the checklist. Proposed items: - add autoscaler cool-down of 180s after scale-up, - explicit pre-warm step for warm pool replicas, - traffic shift policy to prefer partial-slice migration over full-slice failover, - observability queries for early detection.

shera: +1. Also add an abort condition for traffic shifts if p50 latency > 400ms for 2 consecutive minutes.

mike: Can we show the commands/log snippet that identified the kubelet restarts? Put it in the runbook appendix.

elaine: paste: ```
kubectl --context sfo get events --field-selector reason=KubeletRestarted -o json | jq '.items[] | {node:.involvedObject.name, ts:.lastTimestamp, msg:.message}'
```

elaine: Sample log lines: "kubelet[2045]: E0607 12:34:22 kubelet_node_status.go:573] NodeController detected kubelet restart" x6

nate: For cooldown: recommend implementing a token-bucket guard on the autoscaler: allow 1 scale-up per 3m for GPU nodegroups, burst=1. That reduces overlap risk. Also add a short backoff for pod eviction controller when node flaps.

amanda: I'll draft language. Who owns rolling this? ops-lead?

ops-lead: Ops will take ownership of the cooldown policy and the traffic-shift abort condition. Amanda will draft doc updates; Elaine will include the command snippets and logs. Nate, can you prototype the autoscaler token-bucket today and share a quick config? Priority P1 for runbook updates.

nate: Yep — prototyping now. Tentative config: `scaleCooldownSec: 180`, `maxBurst: 1`, `refillRate: 1/180s` (will put as HCL/terraform patch).

shera: Also let's add a short checklist for post-incident triage: 1) confirm reserve pool ordering, 2) check node-restart rate, 3) run weighted-shift dry-run, 4) mark affected slices for increased monitoring for 24h.

amanda: Draft PR URL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-runbooks/pull/542 — includes checklist + new cooldown section + observability queries. I'll add an action table.

mike: Nice. Can we include the alert thresholds you'll add? I want to make sure paging is reasonable.

amanda: Proposed alerts: - SFO_NODE_RESTART_RATE > 3/min -> paged to infra oncall, - SFO_POD_EVICTION_RATE > 2%/5m -> paged, - REALTIME_P50_LATENCY > 400ms for 2m -> page.

ops-lead: Add runbook step: if realtime_p50 > 400ms during shift, immediately rollback weights and open emergency channel and tag @platform-sre.

elaine: Confirmed we should also add a quick script to revert traffic: `infractl traffic shift revert --route realtime --region sfo` — I'll add to appendix.

shera: Action items: 
- ops-lead: own rollout of autoscaler cooldown (ETA tomorrow EOD)
- nate: prototype and post TF patch (ETA today COB)
- amanda: PR author and add alerts/appendix (ETA today EOD)
- elaine: paste log snippets + revert script into PR (ETA today noon)
- mike: verify alert thresholds with oncall (ETA tomorrow morning)

ops-lead: I'll also schedule a 30-min post-incident sync tomorrow 10:30 to validate the changes and set a 72h elevated monitoring window.

mike: One more ask — let's run a DRY_RUN of the weighted-shift script in staging with a synthetic node-restart pattern to validate guard behavior.

nate: I'll spin up a test this afternoon and share results in #eng-sre.

shera: Thanks everyone. Closing thread for now — will update when PR is merged and prototype validated. :white_check_mark:
